detail.longDescription: I’m using SQLAlchemy 2.x with PostgreSQL and declarative models. I have a parent-child relationship between User and Testimonial . from __future__ import annotations from datetime import datetime from sqlalchemy import String, ForeignKey, DateTime, func, create_engine from sqlalchemy.orm import ( DeclarativeBase, Mapped, mapped_column, relationship, Session, ) class Base(DeclarativeBase): pass class User(Base): __tablename__ = "users" id: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String, primary_key=True) testimonials: Mapped[list["Testimonial"]] = relationship( "Testimonial", back_populates="user", cascade="all, delete-orphan", ) class Testimonial(Base): __tablename__ = "testimonials" id: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String, primary_key=True) user_id: Mapped[str] = mapped_column( String, ForeignKey("users.id", ondelete="CASCADE"), nullable=False, ) user: Mapped["User"] = relationship( "User", back_populates="testimonials", ) created_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column( DateTime(timezone=True), server_default=func.now(), nullable=False, ) I understand that this part: cascade="all, delete-orphan" is SQLAlchemy ORM-level cascade behavior. But I also added this database-level foreign key behavior: ForeignKey("users.id", ondelete="CASCADE") Why do I need both? Specifically: Is ForeignKey(..., ondelete="CASCADE") redundant if relationship(..., cascade="all, delete-orphan") is already defined? If I delete a user using SQLAlchemy ORM like this: session.delete(user) session.commit() does SQLAlchemy use the ORM cascade, the database cascade, or both? If I delete a user using raw SQL directly in PostgreSQL: DELETE FROM users WHERE id = 'some-user-id'; will the ORM cascade run? I assume not, because the ORM is not involved. In that case, is the database-level ON DELETE CASCADE required to avoid orphaned rows or foreign key errors? What is the recommended pattern when using both database-level ON DELETE CASCADE and SQLAlchemy ORM relationships? Should I also use passive_deletes=True ? For example, should this: testimonials: Mapped[list["Testimonial"]] = relationship( "Testimonial", back_populates="user", cascade="all, delete-orphan", ) become: testimonials: Mapped[list["Testimonial"]] = relationship( "Testimonial", back_populates="user", cascade="all, delete-orphan", passive_deletes=True, ) I searched the SQLAlchemy documentation, but I’m still confused about the exact difference between: ForeignKey(..., ondelete="CASCADE") and: relationship(..., cascade="all, delete-orphan") Are they protecting against different scenarios? Is one optional? What happens if I remove either one?
